item.title: Jameson’s Distillery Experience Makes Its Port Harcourt Debut
item.description: Three days of whiskey discovery, live music, skating, fashion and games brought the Garden City together over Independence Weekend. Port Harcourt came alive with the Jameson spirit as the Jameson Distillery Experience came to the city for the first time. It took place at Yakubu Gowon Stadium from 1 to 3 October 2026. Over the three days, the experience brought together music, fashion, food, whiskey discovery, skating and games, creating a lively gathering for guests over Independence Weekend. Bringing together Jameson’s Irish heritage and the unmistakable Naija spirit of Port Harcourt, the event offered guests different ways to connect with the brand, discover its story and enjoy a weekend of entertainment, creativity and shared experiences. Across all three days, whiskey education remained an important part of the experience, giving guests insight into Jameson’s heritage and craftsmanship. Food and fashion also added to the atmosphere, allowing guests to enjoy different aspects of the gathering while connecting with one another. Each day featured a distinct experience, delivered in partnership with communities and platforms that brought their own energy and expertise to the programme. Day One: Skating, Music and Energy with Plus2.34 and Voltage District The experience opened with a celebration of skating, music and creative expression in partnership with Plus2.34 and Voltage District. The two communities brought their connection to skating and music to the event, creating a lively atmosphere where guests could watch the skaters in action, enjoy live performances and connect through shared interests. The day’s entertainment featured performances by Sons of Ubuntu, Black Dave, WeAreAllChemicals and Ifeme, alongside DJ sets that kept the energy going. Guests also took part in interactive games, adding friendly competition to the opening day’s programme. Day Two: Games, Competition and Good Music with Game Fiesta Day two brought a playful and competitive atmosphere dubbed “Play City” through Game Fiesta, which turned familiar games into opportunities for guests to interact, compete and have fun together. Guests had different ways to participate, challenge their friends and enjoy the experience beyond the music. Music was another major highlight of the day, with Peruzzi delivering a standout performance. DJ Kaydee, DJ Faithful and DJ Diamond took to the decks, while Hypeman Mayor and Pandora kept the atmosphere lively. Real Chuksy and Annie Drumz added to the day’s entertainment, bringing together live music, DJ sets and games for an engaging Jameson experience. Day Three: Water Games and Entertainment with Whetlvnd The final day introduced a different kind of fun through Whetlvnd, which brought its waterpark-inspired experience to Jameson Distillery. item.title: Lagos Fashion Week 2026 Kicks Off Today! Dates, Venue, Designers & What to Wear
item.description: Lagos Fashion Week street style features showing tiered ruffles, tailored white co-ords, and structured Aso-Oke dresses. Clear your schedules and start ironing out those statement fits— Lagos Fashion Week 2026 officially starts today! From Wednesday, 28th October to Sunday, 1st November 2026, the fashion capital of Africa transforms into a high-energy hub of runway shows, street style spectacles, and creative exchanges. Organised by Style House Files, Africa’s premier fashion platform is back to connect local designers, international buyers, media, and style lovers from across the globe. The theme for the 2026 season is “CRAFTED: Heritage. Innovation. Circular Futures.” This year focuses heavily on pushing sustainable, locally rooted craft straight into the global spotlight. Through initiatives like Green Access and the Fashion Business Series, the event highlights zero-waste tailoring, circular design, and modern interpretations of traditional African textiles—from handwoven Aso-Oke and Akwete to indigo-dyed Adire. Whether you are pulling up to the tents in person or following every outfit update online, this complete guide breaks down everything happening this season—from venue details and designer expectations to the street style cues you need to know. Runway mainstays like Lisa Folawiyo , Andrea Iyamah , Ejiro Amos Tafiri , Ugo Monye , Fruché , and Abiola Olusola will be delivering season-defining moments alongside coveted labels like Christie Brown , Cute Saint , Bloke , and Emmy Kasbit . Meanwhile, the Green Access cohort will present sustainable, forward-thinking mini-collections that show how the next generation of African designers is tackling circular fashion. Rather than standard catwalks, several offsite and tent presentations will also showcase raw fabric production, live artisan weaving, and intricate beadwork. Street Style Cues and What to Wear The pavement outside the LagosFW Tents is just as important as the runway inside. Street style stars, content creators,and fashion editors bring their absolute best to Victoria Island. If you are putting your looks together, consider these three styling cues: Reimagined Heritage Fabrics: Think tailored suits, co-ord sets, or corsets cut directly from Aso-Oke or Adire. item.title: Tiwa Savage Is Giving Rock-Chic Glamour in Black Latex and Purple Fur
item.description: Tiwa Savage posing in a royal purple fur coat layered over a black latex catsuit. A glossy black catsuit and a purple fur coat? Tiwa Savage says she knows how to make both work, and work perfectly! And looking at her latest outfit, we have absolutely no reason to argue. The Afrobeats superstar stepped out in a figure-hugging black latex catsuit with a plunging V-neckline, throwing a plush, oversized royal purple fur coat over the look. Because when you’re Tiwa Savage, why settle for one fashion statement when you can make two? And can we talk about the accessories? Chunky gold bangles stacked on her wrists, sculptural gold earrings and a razor-sharp black bob that gave the entire look an extra dose of attitude. Between the glossy latex, the rich purple fur and those bold gold pieces, Tiwa had every detail working in her favour. Tiwa Savage styling a black latex catsuit with a royal purple fur coat and gold hardware. Now, here’s something to borrow from Tiwa’s style book. A fitted catsuit already does a lot for your silhouette, so pairing it with an oversized coat gives the outfit a completely different shape. That contrast between something sleek and something voluminous is what makes the combination so interesting. And rather than reaching for barely-there jewellery, take Tiwa’s approach with chunky metallic pieces that can hold their own against the outfit. Tiwa Savage backstage wearing a black latex catsuit and gold earrings There’s also a little colour lesson here. Black and purple make a gorgeous pairing, particularly when you play around with textures. The shine of the latex against the softness of the fur makes both colours look even richer, while the gold accessories add warmth to the overall look. So, the next time you’re putting together an all-black outfit and wondering what could give it a little extra personality, you might want to take a page out of Tiwa Savage’s book. item.title: Cynthia Erivo & Ayoade Bamgboye Take “Wicked” to LagOz in Hilarious SNL UK Sketch
item.description: Cynthia Erivo and Ayoade Bamgboye posing through traditional beaded door curtains on the set of Nigerian Wicked. If you thought you’d seen every possible spin on Wicked, think again. West End and Broadway royalty Cynthia Erivo recently stepped onto the Saturday Night Live UK (SNL UK) stage to deliver a masterclass in comedy—teaming up with Ayoade Bamgboye to reimagine the magical land of Oz as a chaotic, low-budget Nollywood blockbuster. Titled “ Nigerian Wicked “ and presented by the fictional Holy Ghost Productions (the satirical masterminds behind classic titles like Beyonce’s Revenge and Light Skin, Dark Heart ), the viral sketch is a love letter to Nollywood tropes complete with a gloriously stressful sound mix. In this universe , Elphaba (played with maximum green-paint intensity by Ayoade Bamgboye) and Glinda (brought to life by Cynthia Erivo in a pink tracksuit, blonde wig, and matching cap) are sharing a room stacked with vintage trunk luggage. Their relationship is wonderfully tense , highlighted by an unforgettable moment where Glinda casually slaps Elphaba because she is “very classless” , only for Elphaba to complain that the room smells like egg. Ayoade Bamgboye as Elphaba and Cynthia Erivo as Glinda sitting on set during the Nigerian Wicked sketch on Saturday Night Live UK. Things get even wilder when the duo boards a train to the land of LagOz to see The Wizard (played by Hammed Animashaun ) , who turns out to be completely broke, rocking a “No-lex” watch instead of a Rolex, and offering his guests some off Bailey’s Irish Cream. While Elphaba is simply hoping her magical transformation defies gravity and earns her a “skinny BBL”, Glinda is laser-focused on her ultimate priority: getting her hands on a Birkin bag. Complete with flying monkeys , Professor Goat , dramatic musical interludes , and a full, gloriously long credit sequence introducing Cynthia by her full traditional name— Cynthia Onyedinmanasu Chinasaokwu Owezuke Amarachukwu Echeumuna Erivo ——this sketch is pure comedic gold from start to finish. Watch below *** Photo Credit: Matt Crockett/Instagram The post Cynthia Erivo & Ayoade Bamgboye Take “Wicked” to LagOz in Hilarious SNL UK Sketch appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: MSS Event Tech Academy: Graduates Over 60 Students Building a New Generation of Event Technology Professionals
item.description: Mobile Screens and Sound Limited (MSS) , a leading event technology and production company, in partnership with KolaDaisi University, has graduated over 60 students from the inaugral MSS Event Tech Academy, marking a significant milestone in the company’s commitment to developing skilled professionals for Nigeria’s growing events and entertainment industry. The graduating students completed a 10-week intensive training programme across one of six specialised departments: LED Screen Engineering; Sound Engineering; Camera Craft and Video Production; Light Design and Control; Event Management and Production; and Rigging and Trussing. Speaking at the graduation ceremony, Tunbosun Kola-Daisi , Managing Director of Mobile Screens and Sound Limited, encouraged the graduates to view the milestone as the beginning of their continued professional development. “Graduation should not be seen as the end of learning, but as the beginning of a lifelong journey of growth. The event technology industry continues to evolve, and as technology advances, so must our knowledge, creativity and capacity to adapt. I encourage every one of our graduates to remain curious, keep learning, and continue to sharpen their craft. We are proud of what you have achieved, but we are even more excited about what you will go on to become.” Held at Darlington Hall in Lagos on Tuesday, September 29, the ceremony also served as a practical demonstration of the technical and practical skills acquired throughout the academy. The graduates took responsibility for the event’s technical and production delivery, including event management, LED screens, sound, lighting and camera operations, giving them the opportunity to apply their skills in a live production environment. In recognition of outstanding performance, the five best graduating students will receive employment opportunities with MSS, providing them with a direct pathway into the event technology industry. Prof. Olajumoke Morenikeji , Vice-Chancellor of KolaDaisi University, highlighted the importance of initiatives that connect education with the realities of the professional world. She remarked, “At KolaDaisi University, we believe strongly that the university must remain connected to the realities of the world beyond the classroom. Education must prepare our students not just to seek employment, but also to create value, solve problems, and create opportunities for themselves. This is why initiatives like the MSS Event Tech Academy are important.” The inaugural Academy comes as MSS prepares to mark its 20th anniversary in October, following two decades of work across Nigeria’s event technology and production landscape. During this period, the company has built expertise across the technical and creative disciplines required to deliver major events and live experiences, while contributing to the growth and professionalisation of the sector. item.title: Bukayo Saka Wins Socrates Award at 2026 Ballon d’Or for Humanitarian Work in Nigeria
item.description: Bukayo Saka addresses the audience after receiving the Socrates Award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony. We know Bukayo Saka for what he does with the ball at his feet, but did you know he’s also helping children in Nigeria get access to life-changing medical treatment? The Arsenal forward and England international has funded 120 operations for children in Kano, Nigeria, through his partnership with the charity BigShoe. And now, that work has earned him the Socrates Award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London. The 25-year-old footballer, who was born in Ealing, London, to Nigerian parents, received the honour on Monday, 26 October, at the Palladium Theatre. The Socrates Award recognises football figures who use their influence to support humanitarian causes, and Bukayo’s contributions to children’s healthcare are at the centre of his recognition. Bukayo Saka acknowledges applause at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London. Through his work with BigShoe, Bukayo has helped children living with conditions such as brain hernias and umbilical hernias receive medical treatment. His charitable efforts have also extended to sight-restoration procedures across Africa, supporting children who need access to specialist healthcare. And guess who was there to present him with the award? Burna Boy . The Grammy-winning Nigerian singer joined Bukayo on the Ballon d’Or stage to hand over the trophy, bringing together two familiar names with Nigerian roots for the occasion. Burna Boy congratulates Bukayo Saka on stage after presenting him with the Socrates Award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or. After receiving the award, Bukayo shared a message on Instagram about what the recognition meant to him and the work he hopes to continue. “Some of the best things this year happened both on and off the pitch. Proud of what we’re building. Grateful to receive the Sócrates Award, and continue to make an impact where we can.” For Bukayo, the recognition comes as his work with BigShoe continues to help children access medical care. Beyond his achievements with Arsenal and England, it’s another part of his story that deserves attention. Bukayo Saka speaks at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony with visuals of his medical charity initiatives in Nigeria displayed behind him. *** Photo Credit: Bukayo Saka/Instagram The post Bukayo Saka Wins Socrates Award at 2026 Ballon d’Or for Humanitarian Work in Nigeria appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Burna Boy Suits Up to Present Bukayo Saka With the Socrates Award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or
item.description: Burna Boy shakes hands with Bukayo Saka at the podium during the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony at the Theatre du Chatelet. Photo Credit: Premier League/Instagram When Burna Boy steps out in a suit, you know it’s about to go down! And this time, the Grammy-winning Nigerian singer wasn’t heading to a concert or an awards ceremony to perform. He was at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, where he presented Arsenal and England footballer Bukayo Sak a with the Socrates Award. The ceremony, held on Monday, 26 October, at the Palladium Theatre, saw Burna Boy exchange his usual stagewear for a tailored black suit with subtle metallic embellishments and dark sunglasses. Beside him, Bukayo looked equally smart in a classic black tuxedo and bow tie. It was quite a sight seeing two Nigerian stars from different worlds sharing the Ballon d’Or stage. But there was more to Burna Boy’s appearance than his outfit and the trophy presentation. Before handing Bukayo the award, which recognises footballers for their humanitarian work and contributions to society, Burna Boy spoke about his own efforts to support football development in Nigeria through an academy he established a few years ago. Speaking about his hopes for the future, he said: Something I started a few years ago, just to support the football culture back home. Hopefully, inshallah, one day I’ll come back here to see one of my people getting an award in Ballon d’Or. It was a fitting moment for Burna Boy to share that ambition, especially while presenting an award that celebrates the impact footballers can have beyond the pitch. And with Bukayo Saka receiving the honour, the ceremony brought together two prominent figures with Nigerian roots, one making his mark in music and the other in football. item.title: Walk Away Cancer 12.0
item.description: As cancer continues to affect individuals, families, and communities across Nigeria, the need for greater awareness, early detection, accessible screening, and patient support remains urgent. On Saturday, 31 October 2026, Medicaid Cancer Foundation will host the 12th edition of Walk Away Cancer , an annual initiative dedicated to raising cancer awareness, encouraging early detection, and supporting people affected by cancer. With the theme One Walk, One Fight , this year’s event will bring together individuals, healthcare professionals, corporate organisations, advocates, volunteers, and community groups to strengthen public engagement in cancer prevention and care. Twelve Editions of Advocacy and Impact Over the years, Walk Away Cancer has grown into a platform for public education, community engagement, health screening, and cancer patient support. The 2025 edition recorded more than 20,000 participants, with over 60 partners and 120 volunteers contributing to the campaign. Participants came from 20 countries, reflecting the initiative’s growing reach. The event’s Health Village provided access to essential health services, including 253 mammograms, 274 clinical breast examinations, 368 blood sugar checks, 200 eye screenings, and 45 HPV vaccinations. The campaign also raised and disbursed over ₦100 million in support of 60 cancer patients, helping address some of the financial challenges associated with cancer care. These achievements demonstrate the importance of taking cancer awareness beyond conversations and connecting it with practical services, early detection, and support for patients. The Health Village: Making Prevention More Accessible A major feature of Walk Away Cancer 12.0 will be the Health Village, where participants can access health education, screening services, and information to support informed decisions about their wellbeing. Free HPV vaccination : Eligible children aged nine will have access to free HPV vaccination, courtesy of the FCT Primary Health Care Board. Breast health awareness : Education on breast cancer, the importance of early detection, and the role of appropriate screening. Discounted mammograms : Attendees will receive coupons for discounted mammograms at Medicaid facilities. Preventive health checks : Selected health checks and screening services designed to encourage participants to take a more active role in managing their health. The Health Village is designed to help people move from awareness to action by making health information and selected preventive services more accessible. Supporting Patients Beyond Awareness A cancer diagnosis can place significant emotional, physical, and financial pressure on patients and their families. For many, the cost of investigations and treatment can become a major barrier to receiving timely care. Medicaid Cancer Foundation continues to champion initiatives that connect awareness with patient support, advocacy, and improved access to cancer care. Proceeds from offic

item.description: Anendlessocean poses in front of black wing backdrop graphics for the official cover art of his 2026 album, Freedom. “Who the Son sets free, is free indeed.” That’s the message Anendlessocean is carrying into his next musical chapter, and it feels fitting for an album titled Freedom. The Nigerian singer and songwriter has revealed the 14-track list for the project, due on 30 October 2026, featuring collaborations with Ryan Ofei , Wale Adenuga , Bolu Ajayi and Saelem . There are some familiar titles on the list, including ‘ Revival ’ and ‘ Promises ’, alongside songs such as ‘ Ri’san ’, ‘ Billion , Trillion , Infinity ’, ‘ Qyis ’ and ‘ Lavish ’. The album also makes room for collaborations, with Canadian gospel singer Ryan Ofei joining Anendlessocean on ‘Speak On It ’, Wale Adenuga featuring on ‘ Let the Church Say ’, Bolu Ajayi on ‘ Good Graces ’ and Saelem on ‘ Undignified ’. Freedom follows a run of projects that includes Decagon (2023), Octagon (2024) and Love Is a Machinery (2026). Anendlessocean has built a sound that draws from contemporary R&B and soul while staying rooted in gospel, and this new album brings that musical world into focus across 14 tracks. The full tracklist moves from ‘Ri’san’ through ‘Billion, Trillion, Infinity’, ‘Qyis’, ‘Revival’ and ‘Lavish’ before ‘Speak On It’. The title track, ‘Freedom’, follows, with ‘Let the Church Say’ and ‘Good Graces’ further down the list. ‘Promises’, ‘Heavy’ and ‘Knows My Name’ lead into ‘ Undignified ’, before the album closes with ‘ Blind ’. item.title: Glinda & Elphaba, Nollywood Style! Cynthia Erivo and Ayoade Bamgboye Serve Early-2000s Looks
item.description: Cynthia Erivo and Ayoade Bamgboye posing through traditional beaded door curtains on the set of Nigerian Wicked. If you grew up watching Nollywood films in the early 2000s, you probably remember the low-rise jeans, colourful tops, side bangs, gold jewellery and beaded curtains that featured in so many scenes. Saturday Night Live UK has revisited that familiar visual world in a sketch titled “ Nigerian Wicked ”, with Cynthia Erivo and comedian Ayoade Bamgboye giving Glinda and Elphaba a distinctly Nigerian makeover. Cynthia, who hosted the episode, takes on Glinda in a metallic pink off-the-shoulder top, low-rise jeans with rhinestone detailing and a silver gear-link belt sitting at her hips. The look leans into the era’s love for pink, sparkle and statement accessories, with a quilted pink crossbody bag and pink bow platform heels completing the outfit. Her dark-rooted blonde hair falls into side bangs, while dark lip liner, stacked gold hoops, a nose ring and long red acrylic nails add to the throwback styling. Ayoade Bamgboye as Elphaba and Cynthia Erivo as Glinda sitting on set during the Nigerian Wicked sketch on Saturday Night Live UK. Across from her, Ayoade gives Elphaba a very different take on the same era. Her green face paint and dark brown flip bob establish the character, while emerald tailored trousers, an olive-brown draped cardigan and a turquoise marble cowl-neck top bring the outfit together. She finishes with a green shoulder bag, chunky gold rings and a gold watch, taking the familiar witch character far from the look audiences might expect from Wicked. Cynthia Erivo and Ayoade Bamgboye posing through traditional beaded door curtains on the set of Nigerian Wicked. The setting is just as important to the visual joke. Vintage backdrop prints and beaded door curtains complete the scene, recalling the interiors that appeared in many older Nollywood films. Rather than simply dressing the characters in Nigerian-inspired outfits, the sketch draws on the styling and set details associated with a particular period of Nigerian screen culture. Cynthia, known for her roles in The Color Purple, Harriet and the film adaptation of Wicked, hosted the episode, while Ayoade, a London-born, Lagos-raised comedian and Edinburgh Comedy Award winner, wrote and co-starred in the sketch. Oscar-nominated star Cynthia Erivo and Edinburgh Comedy Award winner Ayoade Bamgboye posing in retro Y2K styling, including metallic pink tops, silver hip belts, dark sunglasses, and green body makeup for their Nigerian Wicked comedy spoof. *** Photo Credit: Matt Crockett/Instagram The post Glinda & Elphaba, Nollywood Style! Cynthia Erivo and Ayoade Bamgboye Serve Early-2000s Looks appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.description: AI is increasingly getting good at doing some tasks, but it can never replace human workers’ judgment Autonomous cars, which may be the safest we have built, keep getting easily avoidable parking tickets. While Waymos crash far less often than human drivers over tens of millions of miles, they’re still terrible at performing basic tasks – keeping out of disabled parking spots and tow-away zones, or steering clear of a church garage during Sunday service, according to the Wall Street Journal . That is the state of AI today: impressively capable at something complex, yet embarrassingly clumsy at something easy. And it has implications for what work will remain human and what will be automated by AI. item.title: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
item.description: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years ago A few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about. Everyone was on it all the time, and yet its reputation had stalled at “don’t trust it”, because it was the “free encyclopedia that anyone can edit”. Clearly people were trusting it, so much so it had become part of the fabric of everyday life since it was founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001. But despite the fact it now has been consulted trillions of times by billions of people (English Wikipedia alone is 5.2bn words long), it inspires an odd lack of curiosity. Even people donating to Wikipedia might say the money was “for the factcheckers”, though there aren’t any – not paid ones, anyway. Meanwhile, the internet in the social media era had begun to feel like a much uglier place, and some digital nostalgia was setting in: here was this holdover that had somehow survived; a website that functions – and even looks – much the same as it did 20 years ago. Continue reading...

item.description: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying the company's Dragon spacecraft is launched on NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station with NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov aboard, Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

item.title: Star Trails
item.description: This long-duration image shows star trails above Earth and the blue lights of fishing boats and the yellow lights of Indonesian cities stretching below the International Space Station as it orbited 258 miles above the Banda Sea.

item.title: Crew-13 Rocket and Spacecraft at Launch Pad
item.description: Ahead of launch of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, with the Dragon spacecraft atop, is vertical at the launch pad of Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026.

item.title: Mac mini M6 review: truly mighty but now more pricey
item.description: Apple’s cheapest desktop computer is no longer a bargain but its newest, fastest chip makes it a pocket powerhouse Apple’s latest Mac mini brings real speed and power for far more than everyday tasks in a practically pocketable form you can fit almost anywhere. The impressive new desktop machine is the first to receive an update to Apple’s latest M6 chip while remaining smaller than a headphones box. It is the cheapest computer Apple sells with an M-series chip, but like every other memory-containing piece of electronics, it has been hit by RAMageddon , driving up the starting price to £899 (€1,049/$899/A$1,449) from the £599 or equivalent of its M4 predecessor. Continue reading...

item.title: NASA's Hubble Telescope Reaches Milestone, Looks for Elusive Supernova
item.description: An image from NASA's Hubble Space Telescope of galaxy cluster MACS J0417 is part of repeated observations to monitor for the reappearance of supernova Athena, which can help astronomers measure the expansion rate of the universe.

COSI Telescope Comes Together
item.description: UC Berkeley engineers and managers watch as the COSI (Compton Spectrometer and Imager) detector assembly is slowly raised from a table in this July 8, 2026, image.

item.title: Artemis III Crew Visits NASA Kennedy's Vehicle Assembly Building
item.description: NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik (left) and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano view progress on the solid rocket booster integration in High Bay 3 inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026.

item.title: Pixel 11 Pro Fold review: the foldable with the best triple camera
item.description: Big screen folder with slick software and advanced AI is just like a regular Android when closed Google’s latest folding phone sticks with its tried and tested design of a traditional phone shape when closed and almost square when open, in the face of new competition from Apple’s squat iPhone fold . The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is Google’s fourth-generation folder and is still one of the only models with a full water and dust resistance rating similar to standard slab phones. It costs from £1,799 (€1,999/$1,899/A$2,799), which is £50 (€100/$100/A$100) more than last year as the pressure of RAMageddon continues to push up prices. Continue reading...

item.title: NASA's Chandra Spots Galactic Gem
item.description: Galaxies are like cosmic gems, each with characteristics including size and shape that make them distinct. A gallery from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory and other telescopes displays a collection of galactic images that showcase this variety.

item.title: Pixel 11 Pro review: Google’s best pocket camera goes customisable
item.description: Solid battery life, snappy performance and quality software make for a great smaller phone with a killer camera Google’s latest Pro phone is out to prove it has the best camera on a smartphone while embracing customisation, allowing you to change the look and feel of your photos far beyond simple filters even if that means making them technically worse. The Pixel 11 Pro packs the best of Google’s hardware and software into a still-pocketable and easy to handle frame, instantly making it a contender for best smaller phone of the year. item.title: Superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
item.description: N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. One of its most distinctive features, however, is the dark, starry gap called a “superbubble,” visible in this Hubble Space Telescope image in the upper central region.

item.title: Lunar Occultation of Venus
item.description: On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight.

item.title: Igniting Roman's Journey
item.description: Now on a three-month, million-mile journey to its final orbit, NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will soon reveal the universe’s darkest secrets. The mission launched at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Aug. 30 aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

item.title: August Lunar Eclipse Rises Over Louisiana
item.description: A lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana. The lunar eclipse was visible throughout much of North and South America and part of Europe and Africa between Aug. 27-28. The Full Moon slipped through Earth’s shadow on Aug. 27, continuing into Aug. 28 for some parts of the world, resulting in the lunar eclipse. At maximum eclipse, the Moon takes on a dramatic dark, ruddy or coppery tint along the covered edge. New Orleans is home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility, where stages for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and structures for Orion spacecraft are produced for the Artemis missions.

item.title: Artemis III RS-25 Engine Processing: #3 Lift
item.description: Technicians prepare to transfer the #2 RS-25 SLS (Space Launch System) rocket engine (front) to the work stand with the #3 engine (back) for integration with the Artemis III core stage rocket on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. During Artemis III, the four RS‑25 engines will launch the Orion spacecraft and its crew of four into low Earth orbit, generating more than two million pounds of thrust at liftoff.

item.title: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Launches
item.description: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket with NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Telescope on board is seen transiting the sun during launch from Launch Complex 39A, Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026, at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

item.title: NASA's Artemis II Crew Receives Congressional Space Medal of Honor
item.description: President Donald J. Trump awarded NASA astronauts Victor Glover and Christina Koch, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen, and NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman with the Congressional Space Medal of Honor on Aug. 28, 2026, at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

item.title: Astronauts Anil Menon and Sophie Adenot on Spacewalk
item.description: From left, Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA (partially obscured and wearing the spacesuit with a red stripe on the legs) and Sophie Adenot of ESA (European Space Agency) work together during a six‑hour and 23‑minute spacewalk outside the International Space Station.

item.title: NASA's B777 Gets New Coat of Paint
item.description: NASA's Boeing 777 returns to the agency's Langley Research Center after receiving a new paint scheme.

item.title: Colorful Collage of Tarantula Nebula
item.description: Like a collage made of layered sheets of colored cellophane, a vibrant new image layers observations of a famous star-forming nebula from NASA space telescopes. The resulting cosmic “craft” reveals new details about the star formation region known as 30 Doradus, or the Tarantula Nebula.

item.title: Perseids Meteor Shower
item.description: The constellation Orion is framed by two Perseid meteors on Aug. 12, 2018, in Cedar Breaks National Monument, Utah.

item.title: 2026 Total Solar Eclipse in Spain
item.description: A total solar eclipse is seen from San Millán de los Caballeros, Spain, Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026.
